title: UAE Flood Resilience Spending by Emirate (2020-2025)
required_metrics: Annual flood resilience budget (AED or USD) for Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and other emirates, 2020-2025
Source: government budget documents, municipal announcements
comparison_set: By emirate (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, etc.) and year
preferred_sources: Abu Dhabi Department of Municipalities and Transport
search_queries: UAE flood management budget by emirate
data_quality_rule: Use official budget figures where available; if only total infrastructure spending is found, apply a documented climate adaptation share and mark as estimate.
narrative_role: Establishes the market size and growth trajectory of UAE flood resilience investments, segmented by emirate, to justify the opportunity.
pre_exhibit_context: The report claims that UAE municipal budgets for flood resilience are growing at a double-digit rate due to recent storm events.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Dubai and Abu Dhabi dominate spending, with a clear upward trend, validating the near-term procurement window.

title: Annual Flood Damage Costs in UAE (2015-2024)
executive_question: How severe is the storm impact driving demand?
required_metrics: Annual flood damage cost (USD) in UAE, 2015-2024
Number of flood events per year
preferred_sources: Insurance industry reports (e.g., Swiss Re, Munich Re)
data_quality_rule: Seek at least 4 annual observations; if only two endpoints are found, use CAGR to interpolate and clearly mark as estimates.
narrative_role: Quantifies the escalating storm impact, providing the urgency for flood-resilience investments.
pre_exhibit_context: The report asserts that Gulf cities face escalating storm impact, creating demand for flood-resilience systems.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Flood damage costs have risen sharply, especially in 2024, underscoring the need for investment.

title: Cost Comparison: Chinese vs. Western Flood Barrier Systems
required_metrics: Unit cost (USD per meter or per system) for Chinese and Western flood barriers
comparison_set: Chinese vs. Western suppliers (e.g., Fibertex, Flood Control International, local UAE firms)
search_queries: flood barrier cost comparison China vs Western
data_quality_rule: Use comparable specifications; if exact prices are not public, use indicative ranges from industry reports and mark as estimates.
narrative_role: Demonstrates the cost competitiveness of Chinese technologies, a key driver for adoption.
pre_exhibit_context: The report hypothesizes that Chinese flood-resilience technologies are cost-competitive by 30-50% compared to Western alternatives.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Chinese systems offer a significant cost advantage, making them attractive to budget-conscious UAE buyers.
